--- title: Getting Equivalent Results from `glmnet` and `CVXR` author: Anqi Fu and Balasubramanian Narasimhan categories: [] tags: [] params: mode: ignore testdata_dir: test_data/1.9.3 data_dir: glmnet_equivalence --- ::: {.cell} ::: ::: {.cell} ::: ## Introduction We've had several questions of the following type: __When I fit the same model in `glmnet` and `CVXR`, why are the results different?__ For example, see [this](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/51279485/a-comparison-between-cvxr-and-glmnet-elastic-net). Obviously, unless one _actually_ solves the same problem in both places, there's no reason to expect the same result. The documentation for `glmnet::glmnet` clearly states the optimization objective and so one just has to ensure that the `CVXR` objective also matches that. We illustrate below. ## Lasso Consider a simple Lasso fit from the `glmnet` example, for a fixed $\lambda$. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} set.seed(123) n <- 100; p <- 20; thresh <- 1e-12; lambda <- .05 x <- matrix(rnorm(n * p), n, p); xDesign <- cbind(1, x) y <- rnorm(n) fit1 <- glmnet(x,y, lambda = lambda, thresh = thresh) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` Warning in .resolve_control(control = control, nvars = nvars, deprecated = list(thresh = if (!missing(thresh)) thresh, : Passing 'thresh' to glmnet() is deprecated. Use control = list(thresh = ...) instead. ``` ::: ::: The `glmnet` documentation notes that the objective being maximized, in the default invocation, is $$ \frac{1}{2n}\|(y - X\beta)\|_2^2 + \lambda \|\beta_{-1}\|_1, $$ where $\beta_{-1}$ is the beta vector excluding the first component, the intercept. Yes, the intercept is not penalized in the default invocation! So we will use this objective with `CVXR` in the problem specification. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} beta <- Variable(p + 1) obj <- sum_squares(y - xDesign %*% beta) / (2 * n) + lambda * p_norm(beta[-1], 1) prob <- Problem(Minimize(obj)) result <- psolve(prob, verbose = TRUE) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ────────────────────────────────── CVXR v1.9.3 ───────────────────────────────── ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ℹ Problem: 1 variable, 0 constraints (QP) ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ℹ Compilation: "OSQP" via CVXR::Dcp2Cone -> CVXR::CvxAttr2Constr -> CVXR::ConeMatrixStuffing -> CVXR::OSQP_QP_Solver ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ℹ Compile time: 0.131s ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr} ``` ─────────────────────────────── Numerical solver ─────────────────────────────── ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ----------------------------------------------------------------- OSQP v1.0.0 - The results below should be close, and any differences are minor, due to different solver implementations. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} est.table <- data.frame("CVXR.est" = value(beta), "GLMNET.est" = as.vector(coef(fit1))) rownames(est.table) <- paste0("\\(\\beta_{", 0:p, "}\\)") knitr::kable(est.table, format = "html", escape = FALSE, digits = 3) |> kable_styling("striped") |> column_spec(1:3, background = "#ececec") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}

Below is the `CVXR` formulation, where we use the `logistic` atom as noted earlier in our other example on [logistic regression.](/cvxr_examples/logistic-regression) ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} beta <- Variable(p + 1) obj2 <- (sum(xDesign[y2 <= 0, ] %*% beta) + sum(logistic(-xDesign %*% beta))) / n + lambda * p_norm(beta[-1], 1) prob <- Problem(Minimize(obj2)) result <- psolve(prob) check_solver_status(prob) ``` ::: Once again, the results below should be close enough. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} est.table <- data.frame("CVXR.est" = value(beta), "GLMNET.est" = as.vector(coef(fit2))) rownames(est.table) <- paste0("\\(\\beta_{", 0:p, "}\\)") knitr::kable(est.table, format = "html", escape = FALSE, digits = 3) |> kable_styling("striped") |> column_spec(1:3, background = "#ececec") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
